newsitem.title: USA: Midwest Grain sees Q3 results below Q2.
newsitem.headline: Midwest Grain sees Q3 results below Q2.

text.p: Midwest Grain Products Inc said Wednesday it expects results for its fiscal third quarter ending March 31 to be substantially below second quarter net income of $1,205,000, and only slightly better than last year's third quarter loss of $410,000.
However, Midwest Grain said it is beginning to experience much improved operational efficiencies.

Midwest Grain attributed its weakened earnings to the effects of increased competitive pressures in the company's vital wheat gluten and food grade alcohol markets. Energy costs remained considerably higher than normal during the first two months of the quarter due to increased prices for natural gas.

"Significantly lower grain costs compared to a year ago presently are allowing us to strengthen our competitive abilities through increased production output and efficiencies," said Ladd Seaberg, president and chief executive officer, in a statement.
"Significantly lower grain costs compared to a year ago presently are allowing us to strengthen our competitive abilities through increased production output and efficiencies," Seaberg said.

A combination of seasonal factors and the start-up of new production capacities throughout the alcohol industry have caused prices for food grade alcohol for beverage and industrial applications to decline, Seaberg said.
Increased imports of wheat gluten from the European Union have continued to force down prices of that product, he noted.
Seaberg said he remains hopeful that trade advantages held by E.U. wheat gluten and starch manufacturers will ultimately be greatly reduced or eliminated.

Seaburg noted that an investigation was recently initiated by U.S. Trade Representative-Designate Charlene Barshefsky that will target certain E.U. starch/gluten subsidies. The investigation was prompted by a petition filed by the U.S. Wheat Gluten industry Council in January. The council is also evaluating the possibility of pursuing additional legal remedies, according to Seaberg.
Midwest Grain produces vital wheat gluten, premium wheat starch, alcohol products and flour.
